standard.title: Transformations of shapes
standard.description: Describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations of shapes, using dynamic geometric software where appropriate; recognise what changes and what remains the same, and identify any symmetries
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify and describe line and rotational symmetry (AC9M4SP03). They have not yet performed and described all three transformation types or systematically analysed what is preserved under each.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations; recognise what changes and what remains the same; identify any symmetries.

nodes.label: Translation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and perform a translation and explain what properties are preserved.
nodes.minimum_width: Translate a shape by a given vector; describe the translation in terms of direction and distance; explain that shape and size are preserved.
nodes.typical_width: Perform and describe translations on a coordinate grid; describe using coordinate change notation; verify preservation of size, shape and orientation.
wider: Use dynamic geometric software to perform and verify translations
Investigate translation patterns in cultural designs (textiles, tiling)
success_criteria: Student correctly translates a shape as specified
Student states which properties are preserved under translation

nodes.label: Reflection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and perform a reflection across a given mirror line and identify the line of symmetry.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect a shape across a horizontal or vertical mirror line; describe the reflection; identify the line of symmetry.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect shapes across lines in various orientations; identify lines of symmetry in shapes and patterns; verify reflection using folding or measurement.
wider: Investigate reflection symmetry in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art and design
Use dynamic geometric software to explore diagonal lines of reflection

response_modes.reason: Cultural and artistic contexts for reflection symmetry vary the phenomenon meaningfully — students see that the same transformation type appears across diverse human design traditions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cultural design contexts for reflection symmetry give advancing students authentic, rich investigation material.
success_criteria: Student correctly reflects a shape across a given mirror line
Student identifies the line of symmetry in a resulting image

nodes.label: Rotation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and perform a rotation about a point, specifying the centre, angle and direction.
nodes.minimum_width: Rotate a shape 90° or 180° about a given centre point; describe the rotation specifying direction and angle.
nodes.typical_width: Perform rotations of 90°, 180°, 270°; identify rotational symmetry order in shapes; use dynamic geometric software to verify.
wider: Investigate rotational symmetry in cultural patterns and logos
Combine rotation and reflection: identify shapes with both types of symmetry

response_modes.reason: Rotation is the transformation students find hardest to visualise. Multiple contexts — physical, digital, and pattern-based — help build spatial intuition for the operation.

success_criteria: Student correctly rotates a shape by a specified angle and direction
Student describes the rotation using centre, angle and direction

nodes.label: What changes and what stays the same
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare the three transformations and identify which properties are preserved and which change under each.
nodes.minimum_width: State which properties (shape, size, orientation, position) change or are preserved for each of translation, reflection and rotation.
nodes.typical_width: Compare transformations systematically; apply reasoning to classify a given transformation from its description or image; identify symmetries that arise from combining transformations.
wider: Investigate patterns made by repeating a combination of transformations
Analyse a cultural or architectural design to identify which transformations are present

response_modes.reason: Comparing the three transformations requires all three to be understood individually and then contrasted. This integration node is where the systematic understanding of transformation types is consolidated.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Combined transformation pattern analysis is rich and open-ended for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student correctly states which properties change/are preserved for each transformation
Student classifies a given transformation correctly from its description
